stem:
Qadir must construct an exact $15^{\circ}$ angle using equal-radius arcs and angle bisection.

Which plan is correct?

options.text: Call the answer fifteen degrees only, without building $60^{\circ}$ from an equilateral triangle and then bisecting.
Build a $60^{\circ}$ angle from equal-radius arcs, then stop without bisecting to $30^{\circ}$ and again to $15^{\circ}$.
Construct an equilateral triangle for $60^{\circ}$, bisect to $30^{\circ}$, then bisect again to obtain $15^{\circ}$.
Say that drawing $15^{\circ}$ is what creates the equilateral $60^{\circ}$ angle, instead of starting from $60^{\circ}$ and bisecting twice.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal-radius arcs make $60^{\circ}$; two successive bisections give $30^{\circ}$ then $15^{\circ}$. Naming $15^{\circ}$ alone, stopping after $60^{\circ}$, or reversing the construction order all miss that hinge.
